explanation: Smart pointers are template classes in C++ that manage dynamic memory automatically, ensuring proper resource deallocation and preventing memory leaks. They are essential in modern C++ programming for implementing RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) idioms, simplifying memory management, and enhancing exception safety. Smart pointers like std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr, and std::weak_ptr provide different ownership semantics, enabling developers to write safer and more expressive code without manual delete calls.

example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of modern C++ smart pointers to manage dynamic resources. The first block uses std::unique_ptr to ensure exclusive ownership and automatic destruction of the Resource object when it goes out of scope. The second block shows std::shared_ptr managing shared ownership with reference counting, ensuring the Resource is destroyed only after all shared_ptr instances are destroyed. The third block illustrates std::weak_ptr as a non-owning observer that can safely access the Resource if it still exists. This example highlights how smart pointers facilitate safe, automatic memory management aligned with modern C++ best practices.
